These ten hypotheses come from my prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201 and from reasoning about the cell's connectivity. I have not seen any of the experiment results.

Most of them rest on one structural fact. If edge 0 is `none`, node 1 receives nothing, so edits to edges 2 and 4, which read from node 1, have almost no effect. Edge 3 then becomes the only direct input-to-output path, which makes edits to it matter more. In the same way, if edge 5 is `none`, node 2 is cut off from the output and edge 1 edits are close to neutral. For the hypotheses where the unedited effect would normally be negative (a downgrade), a near-zero effect under the condition counts as "higher".
